question.text: An object moves along the positive x-axis having an initial speed of 2.5 m/s and experiences a constant acceleration of 0.50 m/s².

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Determine the total distance traversed during the initial 2 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Calculate the time needed for its speed to reach 7.5 m/s.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the displacement covered by the object when it attains a speed of 7.5 m/s.

conditions: initial velocity = 2.5 m/s in positive x-direction
uniform acceleration = 0.50 m/s² in positive x-direction

solution.approach: Apply the equations of motion for uniform acceleration to each part in turn.

steps.text: Find the distance in the first 2 seconds using s = ut + ½at².
Find the time to reach 7.5 m/s using v = u + at.
Find the distance covered in reaching 7.5 m/s using v² = u² + 2as.
Collecting the three results gives the full answer.

common_mistakes.text: Finding the distance in the first 2 seconds using s = ut alone and forgetting the acceleration term gives 5 m instead of 6 m.
Finding the time to reach 7.5 m/s using t = v/a and forgetting the initial velocity gives 15 s instead of 10 s.
